title: Liouvillian exceptional points in the emergence of quantum synchronization
authors: Carlos Ortega Taberner, Rosalind E. Cotton, Paul R. Eastham
abstract: The coupling between self-sustained oscillators, such as lasers or polariton condensates, leads to different steady-states in different regimes. Weak coupling allows the oscillators to behave independently, with different frequencies and uncorrelated phases, while stronger coupling can produce synchronization. In classical or semiclassical theories transitions between these steady-states correspond to changes in the topology of the phase space attractors and occur at generalized exceptional points. We investigate the corresponding changes in a quantum theory of coupled lasers or condensates. We show how the different steady-state regimes of the classical limit give rise to distinct forms for the spectra and eigenmatrices of the slow modes of the Liouvillian. By following the spectral flow between the different regimes we show that the synchronization transition is controlled by cascades of exceptional points in these slow modes, protected by a generalized PT symmetry. Our results show how singularities of the quantum Liouvillian control the different dynamical regimes, and give rise to experimental signatures of the synchronization transition which remain well-defined in the few-particle regime dominated by quantum effects.
summary: This theoretical paper analyzes quantum synchronization in coupled systems like lasers by examining the Liouvillian spectrum. It demonstrates that the transition between desynchronized and synchronized states is governed by exceptional points within the slow modes of the Liouvillian. The findings provide a quantum signature for these transitions observable even in the few-particle regime.
main_problem: The paper investigates the quantum analog of synchronization transitions occurring in coupled self-sustained oscillators, focusing on how these transitions are controlled by singularities in the quantum Liouvillian.
main_result: The synchronization transition is shown to be controlled by cascades of exceptional points in the slow modes of the Liouvillian spectrum, which are protected by a generalized PT symmetry.
method: The analysis involves calculating the spectrum and eigenmatrices of the Liouvillian superoperator, comparing results to semiclassical approximations, and analyzing the spectral flow between different steady-state regimes.
model_or_system: The system models coupled lasers or polariton condensates, whose dynamics are governed by a Lindblad form Liouvillian superoperator. The analysis utilizes concepts like limit cycles and the $U(1)$ symmetry inherent in the system.
key_observables: The Liouvillian spectrum (eigenvalues $\lambda$), the slow modes of the spectrum, and correlation functions like $g^{(1)}(	au)$ for single and coupled lasers.
important_parameters: Coupling strength, detuning ($\delta\omega$), and the coherence order ($n$) of the correlations.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the Liouvillian formalism and involves approximations for the inverse saturation operator in some derivations.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the Liouvillian spectrum, showing parabolic branches approaching zero decay rates near the limit cycle, and display the Husimi function for various eigenmatrices.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by establishing the Liouvillian framework for coupled oscillators, analyzing the spectral properties related to the classical limit cycle, and then detailing how the synchronization transition manifests as exceptional point cascades in the quantum spectrum.
why_interesting: This work directly addresses open quantum systems dynamics, using the Liouvillian formalism to map classical nonlinear phenomena (like synchronization) onto quantum spectral singularities (Exceptional Points), which is highly relevant for quantum optics and AMO physics.
